meta.scope: Afghanistan Batch 3 — Exchange rate, women's economic exclusion, and border mobility densification under highly constrained conditions.

candidates.title: Exchange-rate and afghani statistics
candidates.description: Official exchange rates for the afghani against major currencies published by Da Afghanistan Bank. The rate is a central price signal for imports, remittances and domestic prices under limited formal capital flows.

candidates.title: Women’s economic exclusion and labour-force framing
candidates.publisher: Derived from UN Women and labour monitoring sources
candidates.description: Framing of the severe restrictions on women’s participation in education, employment and public life. Women’s labour-force participation is extremely low (single-digit employment rates in recent estimates); the exclusion is projected to impose multi-year cumulative GDP losses and is the single most consequential constraint on recovery.
candidates.notes: Highest-centrality structural and human-capital constraint node under current conditions.

candidates.title: Border mobility and returnee statistics
candidates.publisher: Derived from IOM and related monitoring sources
candidates.description: Statistics on cross-border inflows and outflows, especially with Iran and Pakistan. Large-scale returns and ongoing mobility place pressure on host communities, services and livelihoods; formal trade and informal flows interact with these movements.

candidates.title: Afghanistan exchange–women–border densification meta-node
candidates.publisher: Derived from DAB, UN Women and mobility sources
candidates.description: Meta-node binding exchange-rate statistics, women’s economic exclusion framing, and border mobility/returnee statistics into a coherent monetary–human-capital–mobility layer under highly constrained conditions.
